newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK bus operator sees room for expansion in China.
newsitem.headline: HK bus operator sees room for expansion in China.

text.p: Hong Kong-based bus line operator Kwoon Chung Bus Holdings Ltd sees room for expansion in China, the company said in a flotation briefing on Thursday.

"Improved awareness of road safety in the rapidly developing China major cities and increasing traffic within cities, creates huge demand for quality bus services in China," said executive director Andrew Cheng.
The company intends to issue 59 million new shares at HK$1.80 per share. The public offering would be from September 13 to 19. Dealing in shares will begin on September 25.
The company said it would use proceeds raised from the flotation to expand existing bus services in Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shantou, Dalian and to fund bus ventures in Harbin and Chaozhou.
Executive director Frank Wong said the "contribution from China operation is expected to have a significant growth in coming years when more of its bus ventures begin contributing profit."
Bus operations in Hong Kong currently contribute over 80 percent of the company's turnover, Wong added.
In Hong Kong, Kwoon Chung Bus operates franchised bus routes through its 99.99 percent owned New Lantau Bus Company (1973) Ltd on Hong Kong's Lantau Island.
"We have submitted tender to operate routes linking Chep Lak Kok airport with other part of the Island," Wong said.
The company, with a fleet over 800 buses, also provides shuttle bus services to major housing estates and over 30 schools in Hong Kong.
